topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture and contextualizes the difficulty and significance of the complement system.

topics.label: Foundational architecture and central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational architecture and molecular mechanism of C3 that govern the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how distinct recognition pathways converge on C3 convertase generation to reach the threshold for complement activation.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the primary effector mechanisms through which activated complement destroys pathogens and amplifies the immune response.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how regulatory proteins on host surfaces protect host cells from accidental complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Clinical complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the clinical manifestations and disease presentations resulting from deficiencies in various complement proteins.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores the evolutionary strategies and molecular mechanisms pathogens employ to evade complement-mediated killing.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic wraps up the session on complement and previews the upcoming lecture on the adaptive immune system.
